title: Customer status pulse & reconciliation options: November 20 2029
content:
TL;DR: On 2029-11-20 between ~02:14–03:07 UTC we detected intermittent generation stalls and elevated latency for hosted text-generation routes in eu-west-1 and us-east-2. A subset of requests returned partial outputs or timed out. Root cause: a memcache eviction storm combined with an aggressive autoscaler reaction that caused hot model shards to be repeatedly reloaded during a traffic spike. Impacted customers: multi-tenant hosted API customers using medium/large model families in those regions; estimated 0.9% of total requests globally during the window experienced partial or delayed responses. What we told customers during the event (initial status page snippet):

  • Investigating - Increased latency and partial responses for text generation in eu-west-1 and us-east-2. We are actively routing traffic away from affected hosts and applying mitigations. Updates every 15 minutes.

Current mitigation actions (what ops did):
  1) Temporarily pinned high-traffic model shards to warm pools in affected regions to avoid repeated reloads.
  2) Disabled autoscaler step-down behavior for the model daemon group to prevent oscillation while traffic normalized.
  3) Increased memcache capacity on the hot path and adjusted eviction thresholds to preserve KV caches for active sessions.
  4) Applied targeted routing rules in the smart-router to favor lower-latency model variants while core runtime recovered.

Customer-facing reassurance and suggested actions:
  - For customers experiencing partial outputs: retry once with the same request; our servers will attempt to continue generation on retries. For deterministic replay we recommend using the request id and the replay endpoint (see evidence & verification below).
  - If you rely on structured streaming, consider enabling fallback to non-streaming (batch) for a short window to preserve completeness.
  - If you have strict SLA constraints and cannot accept retries, reach out to your account manager to request prioritized routing to Dedicated capacity.

Evidence & verification package (customer self-serve steps):
  1) Collect request-ids for affected calls (X-Request-Id header).
  2) Use our replay endpoint with the --evidence flag: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/replay --data '{"request_ids":["<id1>","<id2>"]}'
  3) We will return a replay report with timestamps, node ids, and final generation outputs. If a replay produces a different result (content drift) we will include the intermediate KV cache state for inspection.

Post-incident customer summary (for status page postmortem):
  Short summary (customer-facing):
    On 2029-11-20 we experienced a region-localized degradation that caused intermittent slow or partial text generation responses for a small subset of hosted API requests. We resolved the issue and applied safeguards to reduce recurrence risk. No customer data was exposed.

  What happened (plain language):
    During a traffic spike in two regions, our caching layer began evicting critical per-session KV cache entries. The autoscaler interpreted the higher CPU/memory signals as host instability and cycled several model-serving hosts. The combination of cache misses and host churn produced repeated model loads which increased latency and in some cases caused streaming responses to stop before completion.

  Root cause (summary):
    - Memcache eviction thresholds were too aggressive for the observed traffic pattern.
    - Autoscaler step-down policy reacted to transient load signals without cross-checking cache warmness metrics.
    - Production observability lacked an aggregated KPI that joins 'model shard reloads' with 'KV cache miss rate', delaying precise detection of the amplification loop.

  Impact details:
    - Regions affected: eu-west-1 (02:14–02:49 UTC), us-east-2 (02:31–03:07 UTC).
    - Roughly 0.9% of hosted generation requests globally returned partial outputs or timed out.
    - No customer secret keys, payloads, or persisted data were exposed or deleted.

  Timeline (high level):
    - 02:12 UTC: First alert - elevated tail latency observed in eu-west-1.
    - 02:14 UTC: Status page posted (Investigating).
    - 02:22 UTC: Ops identified high reload rate on model-serving hosts; started mitigating.
    - 02:30 UTC: Autoscaler mis-step observed; mitigations escalated.
    - 02:40 UTC: Pinning strategy rolled out in eu-west-1; memcache adjustments applied.
    - 02:49 UTC: eu-west-1 latency reduced to baseline.
    - 02:31–03:07 UTC: us-east-2 saw a delayed spike; mitigations completed by 03:07 UTC.
    - 03:20 UTC: Post-incident monitoring confirmed steady-state; status updated to Resolved.

  What we changed (short-term and long-term fixes):
    Short-term (already deployed):
      • Raised memcache eviction tolerance for hot model groups.
      • Temporarily disabled autoscaler aggressive step-down for model-serving nodes.
      • Added temporary routing preference to lower-variant models for best-effort traffic.
    Medium-term (in next 7 days):
      • Implement new metric 'shard-reload-per-minute' and alert when correlated with KV cache miss rate.
      • Add an autoscaler guard that stalls step-down when cache-warmness < threshold.
    Long-term (Q1 roadmap):
      • Rework memcache eviction policy to be workload-aware and implement graded TTLs for session KV entries.
      • Expand pre-warming/resident pools for critical model families based on sustained traffic signals.
      • Productize a customer-facing replay-and-proof API that integrates with status pages for self-service verification.

  Customer choices for reconciliation (pick one):
    Option A - Minimal replay (recommended for most): Provide list of request-ids; we automatically replay and return regenerated outputs and a verification report.
    Option B - Full evidence bundle (for audits): We deliver request traces, node-level logs, and cache snapshots for each request id in a secure bundle. This route requires a signed request from the customer for transfer.
    Option C - Account-level reroute: For customers who prefer dedicated isolation while we onboard long-term fixes, request an account-level prioritized routing to Dedicated or to an alternate region.

  Sample status page messages you can copy: (short, mid, resolved)
    - Short (initial): "Investigating: Some hosted text-generation requests are experiencing partial outputs or increased latency in eu-west-1 and us-east-2. Engineers are applying mitigations; updates every 15 min."
    - Mid (during mitigation): "Update 02:40 UTC: Targeted mitigations rolled out in eu-west-1. Partial responses still possible in some zones; retries recommended."
    - Resolved (final): "Resolved 03:20 UTC: The incident affecting partial/slow generation in eu-west-1 and us-east-2 is resolved. See post-incident summary and available replay options."

  FAQs for customers (quick):
    Q: Is customer data at risk?
    A: No. There was no exposure or deletion of persisted customer data.

    Q: How do I know if my requests were impacted?
    A: Check X-Request-Id for requests between 02:14–03:07 UTC and use the replay endpoint. We can also run tenant-scoped filters if you provide your tenant id.

    Q: Will I be compensated?
    A: We are evaluating SLA credits for tenants materially impacted. If you believe you qualify, file a support case referencing INC-2029-11-20.


Operational notes for Customer Success and Solutions (internal):
  - Priority outreach: identify top 25 customers by request volume routed through eu-west-1 and us-east-2 during window.
  - Provide each with replay-offer template and contact cadence (2 business days).
  - For enterprise customers on Dedicated, offer immediate migration steps and timeline (approx 48–72 hours).
  - Coordinate with SRE for any customer-requested evidence exports; follow security transfer checklist.

Follow-ups and owners: 
  - Ops verification and metrics changes (owner: Priya Gupta, due: 2029-11-27).
  - Customer outreach (owner: Marco Diaz, initial outreach by 2029-11-22).
  - Postmortem doc to Confluence (owner: Elena Park, draft by 2029-11-23; public-facing trimmed summary by 2029-11-24).

Appendix - technical log excerpts (redacted) and example replay report snippet: 
  - Excerpt: node-105 reload-rate=18/min, kv-miss-rate=0.74 -> evictions spike observed at 02:18 UTC.
  - Replay sample line: {request_id: "r-9a7f", original_status: "partial", replay_status: "complete", replay_node: "node-210", latency_ms: "420"}

Notes to self: Keep the external postmortem high-level and actionable; link to replay API docs and provide a fillable form for evidence bundles. Coordinate PR/Comms with Marketing for any social/status page copy.
